paper.title_en: QED radiative effects in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering: traditional and factorized approaches
paper.abstract_en: Semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) of leptons is a vital tool for probing the three-dimensional momentum space partonic structure of the nucleon. Reliable extraction of the intrinsic collinear or transverse momentum dependent parton distributions from SIDIS data requires careful treatment of QED radiative effects beyond the Born level. In this work we perform a detailed comparative analysis of QED effects in SIDIS using the traditional Bardin-Shumeiko approach, augmented by the electron structure function method, and a more recent factorized approach that treats QED and QCD radiation on equal footing. We compare analytical and numerical results of these approaches for the unpolarized $π^+$ electroproduction cross sections off the proton and the Collins and Sivers transverse single-spin asymmetries, and identify the sources of discrepancies between the calculations, which for the cross sections can reach up to $\approx 2\%$, $\approx 7\%$, and $\approx 5\%$ at Jefferson Lab, HERMES, and EIC kinematics, respectively. To provide a unified approach for reliably extracting partonic information from future SIDIS measurements, we propose a hybrid framework that employs the salient features of both frameworks in their respective regions of applicability.
